For positive x, J=-diag(x)(I+tA) is similar to -diag(sqrt(x))(I+tA)diag(sqrt(x)), so strict linear stability iff I+tA positive definite. Independently rebuilt all six adjacency matrices from stated edge lists and used sympy exact determinants/Cramer inverses: G0 det=P Q, P=1-2t-t^2+t^3, Q=1+2t-t^2-t^3, with x=(1-t-t^2,1,1,1-t-t^2,1+t,1+t)/Q; first PD failure at rho~0.4450418679 while every coordinate is positive. For G1 det=(1-t)(1+t-5t^2-3t^3+4t^4), leading principal minors at 2/5 exactly 1,1,21/25,321/625,1281/3125,957/3125 >0; convexity gives PD on [0,2/5]. Cramer numerator of x0 has factor 1-t-4t^2, first zero sigma=(sqrt(17)-1)/8~0.3904 while all others stay positive. Edge swap removes 02,35 and inserts 05,23; degrees (1,1,2,2,3,3) fixed, triangles 0->1 and mean clustering 0->7/18. Independent enumeration of all 2^C(n,2) labeled graphs n=2..5 finds connected totals 1,4,38,728; only 2 five-vertex degree multisets have different triangle counts, with each of their four degree/triangle groups a unique isomorphism class (networkx independent isomorphism verification); exact five-vertex determinants/coordinates give threshold pairs (sqrt3-1)/2<1/2 and 1/3<1/2. Finite census proves sharp minimal n<=5; continuous thresholds follow from exact algebra and positive-definiteness reasoning rather than finite sampling.

value.rationale: A degree-preserving switch is precisely the local operation used in studying clustering versus competitive-network stability, and the first loss of strictly positive linearly stable equilibrium is a natural ecological dynamical invariant. A single elementary triangle creation causes the opposite local effect to a published ensemble association, distinguishing an interior spectral loss from boundary extinction. Proving six is the smallest possible connected order strengthens an otherwise isolated witness into a sharp structural boundary; all four five-vertex graph-family comparisons are nonvacuously classified. This is a motivated negative boundary result, not a claim of refuting the statistical study or of new general ecological dynamics.
